title: How do we simplify these twelve expressions?
description: Twelve expressions in p, q, c and d are simplified by grouping like terms, opening a bracket that has a minus sign before it, and keeping unlike terms apart. A few are checked by putting numbers in place of the letter-numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: group the like terms, and open a bracket with a minus sign before it by changing every sign inside. Watch for students who change only the first sign inside a minus bracket.

video_script.why: A learner uses the way the book checks claims about simplifying to simplify twelve expressions.
video_script.substitution: the book's twelve expressions, each simplified by grouping like terms and opening any bracket with its sign
video_script.anchor: the twelve expressions of the book in p and q, and in d and c
video_script.payoff_line: Every expression is now in its simplest form, and one of them is zero.

final_answer.spoken: four p; three p plus q; two p; two p minus two q; two q; zero; minus two q; minus d; minus c; c; two d minus c; d minus two c

maths_rules: p + q - p + q = (p - p) + (q + q) = 2q
p + q - (p + q) = p + q - p - q = 0
2d - d - (d - c) = 2d - d - d + c = c
video_script.design: The twelve expressions stay on the board in groups; each group is simplified by grouping like terms, and a few are checked by putting numbers in.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; twelve expressions in p and q, and in d and c, in two columns

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the twelve expressions are written
marks.pq: the expressions in p and q are lit
marks.dc: the expressions in d and c are lit
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the expressions

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book. It gives twelve expressions to simplify.
<bookmark mark='pq'/>The first seven use p and q. Some of them have a bracket.
<bookmark mark='dc'/>The last five use d and c. One of them has a bracket too.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What will each expression simplify to?

beats.on_screen: the twelve expressions stay on the board
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: group like terms and add their numbers; the minus sign before a bracket changes every sign inside

marks.like: like terms are circled in matching colours
marks.minus: the minus sign before a bracket flips the signs inside
marks.same: the claim-checking rules from the book appear faintly behind

narration: <bookmark mark='like'/>We group the like terms, and add their numbers.
<bookmark mark='minus'/>The minus sign before a bracket changes the sign of every term inside it.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We work the same way as the claims in your book.

beats.on_screen: Given: twelve expressions in p, q and in d, c
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, twelve expressions in p and q, and in d and c.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to simplify each expression.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: p + p + p + p = 4p;  p + p + p + q = 3p + q;  p + q + p − q = 2p + (q − q) = 2p

marks.four: p + p + p + p = 4p is written
marks.three: p + p + p + q = 3p + q is written
marks.zero: p + q + p − q = 2p + (q − q) = 2p is written

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step one. Four p's added make four p.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three p's and a q make three p plus q, as q is unlike p.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>In p plus q plus p minus q, the q and minus q cancel, which leaves two p.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: p − q + p − q = 2p − 2q;  p + q − p + q = (p − p) + (q + q) = 2q;  p + q − (p + q) = p + q − p − q = 0;  p − q − p − q = (p − p) + (−q − q) = −2q

marks.d: p − q + p − q = 2p − 2q is written
marks.e: p + q − p + q = (p − p) + (q + q) = 2q is written
marks.f: the bracket opens, p + q − p − q = 0 is written
marks.g: p − q − p − q = (p − p) + (−q − q) = −2q is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>Step two. Minus q twice and p twice give two p minus two q.
<bookmark mark='e'/>In p plus q minus p plus q, the p's cancel. The q's add up to two q.
<bookmark mark='f'/>For p plus q minus the bracket p plus q, open the bracket. That gives p plus q minus p minus q, which is zero.
<bookmark mark='g'/>In p minus q minus p minus q, the p's cancel. The minus q's make minus two q.

marks.j: the bracket opens and 2d − d − d + c = c is written

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step three. Take two d minus d minus d minus d. Two minus one minus one minus one is minus one, which gives minus d.
<bookmark mark='i'/>In two d minus d minus d minus c, the d's make zero, which leaves minus c.
<bookmark mark='j'/>For two d minus d minus the bracket d minus c, open the bracket. The sign of c changes, and the d's cancel, which leaves c.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 2d − (d − d) − c = 2d − 0 − c = 2d − c;  2d − d − c − c = d − 2c

marks.k: (d − d) = 0 is written, then 2d − 0 − c = 2d − c
marks.l: 2d − d − c − c = d − 2c is written

narration: <bookmark mark='k'/>Step four. In the bracket d minus d, the answer is zero. Two d minus zero minus c is two d minus c.
<bookmark mark='l'/>In two d minus d minus c minus c, the d's leave d. The c's make minus two c.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, check with p = 2, q = 1, d = 3, c = 1: p − q + p − q = 2 and 2p − 2q = 2;  p + q − (p + q) = 0;  2d − d − (d − c) = 1 = c;  2d − (d − d) − c = 5 = 2d − c;  2d − d − c − c = 1 = d − 2c

marks.nums: 2 replaces p, 1 replaces q, 3 replaces d and 1 replaces c
marks.pq: 2 and 2, then 0, appear for the p and q expressions
marks.dc: 1 and 1, 5 and 5, 1 and 1 appear for the d and c expressions

narration: <bookmark mark='nums'/>Step five, check some with p as two, q as one, d as three and c as one.
<bookmark mark='pq'/>Two minus one plus two minus one is two, and two p minus two q is two. The bracket one gives zero.
<bookmark mark='dc'/>The d and c expressions give one, five and one. The simplified forms give the same.

marks.ans: the twelve simplified forms are written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every expression is now in its simplest form, and one of them is zero.
